content.text: The redline validated. Submitting the finding.

input.quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and expenses of investigation (collectively the "Losses") which Sparkling or any of its respective officers or directors may incur due to a breach of this warranty. Sparkling shall notify Garman in writing of any such claim within ten calendar days of a responsible officer of Sparkling becoming aware of such claim.
input.rationale: Section 13 (continuing at p0090) does contain a Garman-side IP indemnity tied to breach of its ownership/non-infringement warranty, with procure/modify/replace remedies (p0091-p0093) and no fee-only refund escape, and Section 15 expressly carves breaches of Section 13 out of the liability cap (p0105) with survival confirmed in Section 18. So the walk-away and the "indemnity absent / IP excluded" triggers are not met, and there is no offsetting Sparkling indemnity to narrow. However, the clause falls short of our preferred position in four respects: (1) it is indemnify-and-hold-harmless only, with no obligation to defend third-party claims; (2) it covers only Sparkling and its officers and directors, not our affiliated companies, even though Section 2 licenses the Work for use by Sparkling affiliates at Authorized Locations; (3) there is no claim-handling procedure (control of defence, no settlement binding us without consent, cooperation), and the sole procedural term is a hard ten-calendar-day notice requirement with no materiality or prejudice qualifier, which risks being read as a condition precedent forfeiting the indemnity; and (4) the indemnity is limited to breach of the IP warranty and gives us nothing for Garman's breach of applicable law, unauthorized access to or disclosure of our data or Confidential Information caused by Garman, or Garman's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. The redline inserts a single additional paragraph after p0093 supplying the defence duty, affiliate coverage, the standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and the missing misconduct triggers, leaving the existing warranty indemnity and remedies intact as the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position.

proposal.summary: Add express defence obligation, affiliate coverage, claim-handling procedure and indemnity cover for Garman's breach of law, data breaches and wilful misconduct to Section 13.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 13 gives us a hold-harmless for breach of the IP warranty but no duty to defend, no cover for our affiliates, no claim-handling procedure, and nothing for Garman's own breach of law, data breaches or wilful misconduct. We have added those items and clarified that a late notice only cuts back the indemnity to the extent Garman is materially prejudiced; if Garman prefers, we can accept the indemnity being subject to a super-cap of 3x annual fees instead of the current Section 15 carve-out.

ops.text: In addition, Garman shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Sparkling and its affiliated companies from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting Losses, to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Work, or Sparkling's use of the Work as permitted by this Agreement, infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right of any Person; (ii) Garman's breach of applicable law; (iii) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Sparkling's data or Confidential Information caused by Garman; or (iv) Garman's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Garman shall have control of the defence and settlement of any such claim, provided that Garman shall not settle any claim in a manner that imposes any obligation on, or requires any admission by, Sparkling without Sparkling's prior written consent, and Sparkling may participate in the defence with counsel of its own choosing at its own expense. Sparkling shall provide reasonable cooperation at Garman's expense, and any failure to give notice of a claim under this Section 13 shall relieve Garman of its obligations only to the extent Garman is materially prejudiced by such failure.
